test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 20 Sept 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Plaster of Paris should be stored in sealéd containers.

Which of the following is the correct explanation for the given assertion?

options.text: It turns into a hard solid after reacting with moisture present in air.
It decomposes in the presence of sunlight.
It decomposes in the presence of oxygen.
It turns into hard solid after reacting with oxygen present in the air.

solution:
The correct answer is __It turns into a hard solid after reacting with moisture present in air.__

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• The most common use for the substance "**Plaster of Paris**" is for creating **sculpting materials and gauze bandages.**
 
• **Plaster of Paris** is synonymous with **gypsum plaster**, another common name for the substance.
 
• This is the chemical formula for Plaster of Paris- **CaSO4. H2O**
 
• Plaster of Paris is **calcium sulfate**, and a hard substance called gypsum is produced when crystallization water is added.
 
• It may react with any moisture in the air if it were not stored in a **moisture-proof container**.
 
• **Upon combined with water**, it transforms into **gypsum**, **a hard substance** having quite different characteristics from the plaster of Paris.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Some of the things you can do with the plaster of Paris are the following:
 
 
• It is used **in medicine to make plaster casts** that keep broken bones from moving.
 
• It is also used** to make and hold parts of ceiling plasterwork** that are used for decoration. So, it is used to make **decorations and toys**.
 
• It can also be used **to level out surfaces.**
